questions.stem: What does the term NoSQL actually mean?
questions.explanation: NoSQL means Not-Only-SQL, so standard SQL can still be used with NoSQL databases, with minor syntax changes.

questions.stem: Which four types of NoSQL database came onto the surface with the introduction of Big Data?
questions.explanation: In the past there was only one database type, RDBMS (SQL). With Big Data, four more types of NoSQL database appeared: Key-Value, Columnar, Document and Graph DB.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT given as an example of a SQL/RDBMS database?
questions.explanation: Examples of SQL database types are Oracle, DB2, Teradata, SQL Server and MySQL. Hive is a wrapper over files in HDFS, not an RDBMS.

questions.stem: What storage can NoSQL databases use in addition to server OS file systems such as EXT and FAT?
questions.explanation: In contrast with SQL/RDBMS databases, which use server OS file systems like EXT and FAT, the new NoSQL databases can additionally use HDFS.

questions.stem: Among the five data stores in Hadoop (Hive, Key-Value, Columnar, Document and Graph DB), which one uses only HDFS as its storage?
questions.explanation: Hive only uses HDFS as storage. The Key-Value, Columnar, Document and Graph databases can use either OS file systems or HDFS.

options: A wrapper on top of files sitting in HDFS that shows the files in the shape of tables for ease of use
A relational database that replaces Oracle in Hadoop
A graph database that stores entities as nodes and relationships as edges
A file system used by SQL Server
A key-value cache for HDFS metadata
questions.explanation: Hive is a wrapper on top of files sitting in HDFS. It shows files in the shape of tables for ease of use for users.

questions.stem: How does a Key-Value database store data?
options: As tables with rows, columns and schemas
As a collection of key-value pairs in which the key normally serves as a unique identifier
As documents with data type descriptions and values
As nodes and edges with unique identifiers
As columns rather than rows for analytical processing
questions.explanation: A key-value database stores data as a collection of key-value pairs, in which a key normally serves as a unique identifier. Both keys and values can range from simple objects to complex compound objects.

questions.stem: Why is a Columnar database suitable for analytical query processing and data warehouses?
options: Because it stores entities as nodes and relationships as edges
Because it requires no SQL and no tables
Because it stores data by columns rather than by rows
Because it uses only HDFS as its storage
Because it stores each record as a document
questions.explanation: A columnar database stores data by columns rather than by rows, which makes it suitable for analytical query processing and thus for data warehouses.

questions.stem: What do NoSQL Document databases use instead of the tables, columns, rows, schemas and tabular relations of relational databases?
options: Flat files in HDFS shown as tables
Documents with data type descriptions and values
Star schemas with fact and dimension tables
questions.explanation: NoSQL document databases are based on a model that does not require SQL and tables. Instead they use documents with data type descriptions and values.

questions.stem: How is a Graph database characterised in comparison with a relational database?
options: It stores data by columns and is best for data warehouses
It uses documents rather than tables
It has no unique identifiers on its entities
It can only use OS file systems, never HDFS
It is multi-relational in nature, whereas relational tables are loosely connected
questions.explanation: In a Graph database the entity is stored as a node and the relationship as an edge, each with a unique identifier. Compared with a relational database where tables are loosely connected, a Graph database is multi-relational in nature.
